question: Are monarch larval hosts with independently classified high versus low performance redistributed to different numbers of alien botanical regions, after accounting for their native range breadth and genus?
scientific_non_tautology: Not whether deleting a low-performance host shrinks resource area, but whether external larval performance classification predicts an observed and independently sourced host plant introduction footprint.
prior_exposure: Previously inspected Asclepias curassavica: H3, 97 introduced WGSRPD3 regions.
Previously inspected Araujia sericifera: L3, 24 introduced WGSRPD3 regions.
127-source quality panel H=34 L=42 N=33 U=18 known before WCVP crosswalk.
Comparison is not confirmatory; it follows other exploratory host-quality work.

source.performance: Greenstein, Steele & Taylor 2022 PLOS ONE doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0269701, source S1 Appendix table of 127 plants, downloaded/retained in GitHub Actions run 37736225347 artifact monarch-127-host-quality-independent-source-v01
source.sampling_unit: unique accepted botanical species with exactly one source quality classification and one unambiguous WCVP accepted taxon mapping

performance_classes.high: H1,H2,H3, from independently published qualitative classification
performance_classes.stronger_evidence: H3 versus L3 secondary; not necessarily commensurate sample sizes, and classify by author definition

matching.method: exact WCVP species-level name including accepted species or unique botanical synonym mapped to accepted_plant_name_id
matching.no_extant_nondoubtful_native_distributio: exclude from primary rather than assuming zero
matching.duplicate_to_same_accepted_species: deduplicate only if classifications agree; otherwise exclude conflict, log

primary.population: Asclepias genus; high vs low; retained distinct accepted species, native WCVP regions >=1
primary.outcome: log1p(number of WCVP WGSRPD3 regions classified introduced for species)
primary.effect: difference in native-range-residualized mean log1p introduced counts (high minus low)
primary.null: permute high/low species labels only within native-range quartiles of accepted Asclepias source species, preserving high/low count per stratum

secondary: Raw high/low medians of introduced region count and any introduced range
Strong evidence H3 versus L3 Asclepias only, same method if >=4 per group
Robustness removing known globally distributed H3 Asclepias curassavica BEFORE inspecting the full mapping outcome
Broader Apocynaceae only as descriptive, not pooling other unrelated families
Quality class composition of introduced-only regions from independently classified plants, clearly labeled potential resources rather than observed butterfly colonization
stop_rules: If fewer than 5 independently matched Asclepias high and low, do not test association.
If permutation null cannot shuffle labels across at least two strata, do not report Monte Carlo significance.
If null is not exceeded two-sided or dominated by A.curassavica, do not claim high/low quality predicts globalization.
No opportunistic inclusion of unverified synonyms, N or U as true low.
Do not present phylogenetically correlated quality records as independent experimental studies.
Do not modify main GEB manuscript.
biological_claim_boundaries: Performance class is a literature synthesis, may conflate feeding and survival and evidence quality. H1/H2 not directly equivalent to H3.
WCVP introduced presence is regional plant naturalization, not planted-only occurrence or plant biomass.
A difference in botanical range by quality is a macroecological association; it cannot quantify monarch larval survival, local population growth, competition or causal invasion.
Source taxonomy and introduced distributions may have coverage bias and strong within-genus phylogenetic structure.
Reconstructing any host quality map from same input cannot by itself establish an ecological mechanism. Independent consumer endpoints remain priority.
